events.caption: Apply the smaller impulse to red.
Five times the impulse gives much less than five times the speed.

setup: Compare impulses 2 (red) and 10 (blue). Neither launch reaches speed 2.2.
name: Speed has a limit

oracle.name: Speed has a limit
oracle.law: Each free body obeys \mathbf p=m\mathbf v/(1-|\mathbf v|^2/v_max^2), with v_max=2.2. Forces and impulses add momentum, with diminishing speed gains. Neither launches nor free fall reach the limit, even for added free bodies. Fixed and joint-constrained parts obey ordinary physical laws.
oracle.condition: A force or impulse adds momentum to a free body.
oracle.effect: More impulse yields diminishing speed gains. Speed stays below 2.2.
oracle.scope: The limit also applies to free fall and added free bodies.

reference: Same geometry, masses and scripted actions; the altered program is disabled only in the ordinary-physics reference.
